title: RiskFile: AML risk assessments and audit-ready files for small UK law firms
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: UK regulators are fining small law firms for missing or weak anti-money-laundering risk assessments. RiskFile drafts the firm-wide risk assessment, guides a short client and matter risk assessment for every new matter, and keeps everything in a file ready for an SRA review.
hook: "We do ID checks on every client. But when the SRA asked for our firm-wide risk assessment, we sent a template we downloaded in 2018."
story:
**David is managing partner of a 6-solicitor firm in Leeds** doing conveyancing, wills and small business work. The firm uses an online ID-check tool for every client, so he thought AML was handled. Then the regulator sent a **desk-based review** letter asking for the firm-wide risk assessment, three recent client and matter risk assessments, and evidence of staff training.

The risk assessment was a **2018 template** never updated, and the matter assessments were ticks in a case-management field with no reasons. Firms like his have been fined **from about £2,000 up to the £25,000 maximum** for exactly this. David spends two weekends rewriting documents with a consultant at £150 an hour, and still is not sure every new matter will be done properly from now on.
whyNow: The SRA has said it will "ratchet up" AML enforcement after a wave of fines in 2025, many of them for missing or inadequate firm-wide risk assessments. ID-check tools solve identity, not the written risk assessments the regulator now asks to see.
evidence: The SRA issued about £575,000 of AML fines in six months and said it would "ratchet up" its enforcement [Legal Futures]
Small firms were fined roughly £2,000–7,000 for missing or inadequate firm-wide risk assessments, and several firms got the £25,000 maximum for traditional firms [Legal Futures / Solicitor News]
UK law firms were hit with record AML fines in 2025 [FinTech Global]
ID checks are already sold per check: Thirdfort lists about £15 per biometric ID check; Amiqus reportedly has a £500/month minimum (competitor-published figure) [Thirdfort / FigsFlow]
71–75% of solo and small-firm lawyers use AI, mostly generic tools [Clio 2026 Solo and Small Legal Trends Report]

whyReal.title: Fines are public and frequent
whyReal.text: The SRA publishes every fine with the firm's name, so small firms see their peers punished for paperwork, not for laundering.

whyReal.title: ID tools leave a gap
whyReal.text: Thirdfort, Amiqus and others check identity and source of funds. The written firm-wide assessment, matter-level reasoning and yearly review are still Word documents.

whyReal.title: A narrower, safer version of law-firm intake
whyReal.text: General AI intake for law firms was dropped from the Top 25 because Clio competes. AML files are a specific, regulator-driven job that Clio's intake does not solve.

whyReal.title: Clear buyer with a register
whyReal.text: Every regulated firm is listed on the SRA register, so Jonatan can build lead lists in English from public data.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Small law firms (1–25 fee earners) in England and Wales, especially conveyancing, private client and small commercial practices.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The managing partner or the Money Laundering Compliance Officer (MLCO).

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK (SRA-regulated firms), later Irish solicitors and UK accountants supervised for AML.

solution.title: Firm profile interview
solution.text: a 20-minute guided questionnaire about practice areas, client types, countries, payment methods and delivery channels.

solution.title: Draft firm-wide risk assessment
solution.text: AI drafts the assessment from the answers, mapped to the regulator's guidance and the national risk assessment, with a clear list of controls. The MLCO edits and signs.

solution.title: Matter risk check in 3 minutes
solution.text: for each new matter, a short form produces a risk score with written reasons and the checks required (simplified, standard or enhanced due diligence).

solution.title: Attach evidence
solution.text: upload or forward the ID-check report, source-of-funds documents and notes; everything is stored per matter.

solution.title: Yearly review and training log
solution.text: reminders to review the firm assessment, track staff AML training and keep a dated history.

solution.title: Audit pack
solution.text: one click exports the firm assessment, a sample of matter files and the training log for an SRA review.

must: Client and matter risk assessment form with written reasons
later: Import of Thirdfort or Amiqus reports

techStack: LLM with guidance documents as reference (RAG)
